_comment: Prepared, not run (#11's own text: 'Publish conformance evidence for both collections and a bounded compatibility statement; do not build a second large benchmark'). Execution needs #81's operator demo command, which is in progress (issue-81-operator-demo, w1) and #10's own live Docker run - neither exists yet. This manifest states the exact command each run will use, per the agreed --subject design (orchestrator ruling, msg 1474, relayed to w1): --subject <name> materializes evals/subjects/<name>/subject.json through materialize.py and installs it via DockerBackend.install() into the real container used by #81's demo, then observes discovery via the client's own no-model listing (the same codex debug prompt-input path skillc/exposure.py already uses) - never a model call. The lifecycle and grading demos #81 already has are unchanged: slug-small-fix stays the graded task regardless of --subject.

unsupported_formats_refused_before_selec.claim: an unsupported surface, an unsupported client, or a malformed subject declaration is refused by materialize.Subject.from_dict BEFORE any selection happens, for either subject or any other
unsupported_formats_refused_before_selec.evidence: tests/test_materialize.py::test_a_malformed_subject_declaration_is_refused, 10 parametrized cases (unknown keys, unsupported surface, unsupported client, no client version, an escaping path, a malformed select, and more) - the logic is generic, not subject-specific, so it applies to cpp-codex and mattpocock-skills identically; cited per orchestrator instruction (msg 1474), not re-proven per-subject here

bounded_compatibility_statement: See README.md in this directory for the full statement, which keeps two kinds of evidence separate (codex review of this PR: an earlier draft blurred them into one overclaim). In one line: skillc materialize has ACTUALLY RUN against both subjects on the host with no adapter change; trial.py/verify.py/backend.py/docker_backend.py carry no subject-name branch, by STATIC proof, never by execution; but no full trial (plan, dispatch, capture, grade) has ever been run for EITHER subject through any backend - that gap is exactly what this manifest's two runs are prepared to close, not a gap already closed by the adapter-only evidence or the genericity guard. This says NOTHING about which collection helps an agent more, about task outcomes, or about any paid model call - #10/#12/#26 own those questions, not this manifest.
